keywords: 策略、Operator 和 Group 各管什么
title: Strategy, Operator, and Group roles
summary: Strategy computes signals; Operator schedules strategies; Group holds strategies that share timing. This card names the three roles only—creation, mixing, bases, and lookup are separate cards.
narrative:
In qteasy, three names work together:

- Strategy: given history DataTypes and tunable parameters, realize() returns a trading signal for the current bar.
- Operator: holds strategies, sets how they run (timing and signal_type as construction knobs), and produces a unified signal stream for backtest or live.
- Group: strategies that share the same run timing land in one Group; that Group can mix their outputs with a blender.

This card only answers what each word means. How to construct an Operator, how blender works, which base class to inherit, and how to look up built-in ids are separate strategy topics. Signal-number meanings (target weight versus order size) are a separate card too.
python_code:
import qteasy as qt
op = qt.Operator(strategies='dma', signal_type='pt')
print(type(op).__name__, list(op.groups.keys()))
risk_notes: Ask explains roles only. Creating files, running backtests, and listing every built-in id are other cards or Plan.
